Iran International (English) — "Iran takes US response to cabinet, Hormuz clashes continue". Published 30 September 2026, 13:05 (page timestamp GMT+1 = 13:05 BST). CONFIRMED 30 Sep.
Retrieved via WebFetch. Text below as rendered by the tool; quotes as returned.

US RESPONSE / DIPLOMACY
Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi received US feedback on Iran's seven-day proposal during talks with Qatari mediators in Doha on Tuesday night. According to an official briefed on the talks, the main disagreement concerns "the sequencing of the plan rather than its elements."

Araghchi (Iranian Foreign Minister): "We are awaiting an official response from the United States through the mediators."
Araghchi: "Iran's conditions are entirely fair and reasonable. If the Americans say they want an agreement or a peaceful solution, we have presented that solution."
[Also attributed to Araghchi in the Exa index snippet of this same page: "At present, the only issue is the Strait of Hormuz." — treat as verbatim from this article but flagged as snippet-sourced.]

President Trump suggested Iran would eventually "give up," but indicated that point had not yet been reached.

US SECRETARY OF STATE
Marco Rubio (US Secretary of State) warned that Iran had "openly threatened American interests around the world" and would "face repercussions for any attack or attempted attack."

GOVERNMENT SPOKESPERSON
Fatemeh Mohajerani (Iranian government spokesperson): "We are not afraid of war and we do not run away from negotiations."

HORMUZ
A tanker heading into the Strait of Hormuz was struck by an unknown projectile. UK Maritime Trade Operations reported the incident; authorities investigating.
Hossein Mohebi (Revolutionary Guards spokesman): Iranian forces were "targeting ships every 24 hours" but had "received no US response for some time."

EXECUTIONS (30 Sep)
Ali Hemmati and Majid Nikandish executed over January 2026 demonstrations in Mashhad. Judiciary accused them of involvement in the deaths of four security personnel and of "attacking security personnel, setting buildings on fire and damaging public property."

CURRENCY
Iran's exchange rate crossed 2.5 million rials to the dollar on 30 September, extending a sharp decline that increased import costs and eroded purchasing power.
